summary: Triggers an action on the current screen: save, publish, approve, open a dialog. If it takes the user somewhere else, it is a Link, not a Button.
whenToUse: The user commits an action on this screen: Publish, Approve, Create token, Open pull request.
Primary: the one action you most want the user to take in this view. One per form, dialog or page section.
Secondary: the alternatives next to the primary, like Save as draft or Request changes.
Ghost: low-emphasis actions repeated in lists, tables or toolbars (Edit, View diff), where filled buttons would fight for attention.
Danger: destructive actions (Delete, Revoke access). Usually inside a confirmation dialog.
Size sm in dense rows and toolbars, md everywhere else, lg only for a single call to action on an empty or onboarding screen. Heights follow the density setting.
whenNotToUse: Going to another page or URL: use Link. Links and buttons are announced differently and users expect Cmd+click to open links in a new tab.
Turning a setting on or off: use Switch or Checkbox.
Picking one of several views: use Tabs or an attached ButtonGroup.
More than three actions in one row: keep the main ones and move the rest to a Menu behind an IconButton.

dos.title: Start the label with a verb that names the outcome
dos.text: "Publish tokens" and "Approve change" tell the user what happens before they click.

dos.title: One primary per view, the others step down
dos.text: Hierarchy tells users where to look first. Secondary and ghost carry the alternatives.

dos.title: Show progress with loading, keep the label
dos.text: The button stays in place and focusable, so keyboard users do not lose their position. Change the label to the present participle.

donts.title: Two primary buttons side by side
donts.text: When everything is primary, nothing is. Users hesitate and pick at random.

donts.title: Vague labels
donts.text: "OK" and "Click here" say nothing out of context, and screen reader users often list buttons out of context.

donts.title: Danger for actions that are not destructive
donts.text: Red trains people to ignore red. Keep danger for actions that remove or revoke something.

accessibility: Native button through Base UI: Enter and Space activate it, it is in the tab order, no extra ARIA needed.
The focus ring (focus.ring.color, 2px, offset 2px) shows on keyboard focus only, never on mouse click.
Loading sets aria-busy and aria-disabled, ignores clicks, and keeps the button focusable so keyboard users keep their place.
Disabled removes the button from the tab order and explains nothing. Prefer an enabled button plus a message saying what is missing.
With render={<a href />} the element stays a link (role link), which is right for navigation styled as a button.
Heights are 32/40/48px comfortable and 28/32/40px compact: all above the WCAG 2.2 minimum target of 24px.
contentGuidelines: Sentence case, no trailing period: "Open pull request", not "Open Pull Request."
Verb plus object, two to four words. Drop the object only when context makes it obvious (Save, Cancel).
The same verb follows through the flow: Publish, Publishing, Published.
Name the count on bulk actions: "Delete 3 tokens".

anatomy.primary: Primary variant (steel ink in the bridge brand)
anatomy.icon: Leading or trailing icon, or the loading spinner
anatomy.label: Label
